_note: Multi-file plan: M1 targets walk_register_lint.py, M2 targets tools/run_check.py, M3-M5 target cycle_check.py. mutation_check supports one target per invocation; run it three times (once per target) to verify all 5. The 'target' field names the primary file; per-mutant 'target' overrides the default for M1 and M2.

mutants.name: M1-drop-version-branch
mutants.why: Defect A: removing the version-aware short-circuit collapses back to presence-only check, mis-classifying 0.1 registers as NO_TABLE (false positive, not a defect). Killed by test 1.

mutants.name: M2-pre-schema-counted-bad
mutants.why: Defect B variant: adding PRE-SCHEMA to the bad-status check in judge_register would mis-judge 25 corpus registers as failures. Killed by test 5.
mutants.anchor: bad = [ln for ln in stderr.splitlines() if "\tUNCONFORMANT" in ln or "\tNO_TABLE" in ln]
mutants.replacement: bad = [ln for ln in stderr.splitlines() if "\tUNCONFORMANT" in ln or "\tNO_TABLE" in ln or "\tPRE-SCHEMA" in ln]

mutants.name: M3-assign-fail-not-warn
mutants.why: Defect C promotion: assigning register_result = 'FAIL' instead of collecting a WARN immediately escalates via the pre-wired arm at run_check():424 — halting every cycle that carries a non-conformant register. Warn-first is deliberate; the FAIL arm is the earned-later promotion path. Killed by test 7 (verdict must remain BAR_MET, not escalate).
mutants.anchor:
register_warn = (
                        f"WARN: walk register {resolved_path.name!r}"
                        f" — {reg_status} (non-conformant register; does not block verdict)"
                    )

mutants.name: M4-warn-printed-after-verdict
mutants.why: P8 contract: printing the WARN after the verdict breaks run_check's documented channel fact — its last stdout line would no longer be the bare verdict token. Killed by test 9.

mutants.name: M5-run-check-returns-3-tuple
mutants.why: CONTROL mutant: run_check() returning a 3-tuple raises ValueError at all 40 test_cycle_check.py call sites that unpack exactly 2 values — proving P15's arity guard is real, not assumed. Must be killed by the EXISTING suite, not a new test. A survivor means the arity is unprotected. Selector targets a BAR_MET plan (reaches the final return verdict, 0 path); early-exit tests like test_unparseable_no_block never reach that line and cannot kill this mutant.
